input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN running against us: we would have to give Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms offered to any other technology supplier. It is unlimited in scope, product and duration and has no comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory (open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN in our favour exists to preserve, so the minimal fix is deletion of the obligation.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the most-favoured-nation obligation in Section 7.2: our playbook does not permit us to accept an open-ended commitment to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other supplier, and it conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. If some price assurance is important, we could discuss a narrow MFN limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.
